review_metadata.review_type: bounded scoping review with primary theorem and observation-contract checks
review_metadata.question: Which assumptions permit or preclude joint-distribution, shared-source, or causal-graph recovery from integrated assay data?
review_metadata.discovery: Parent coordinated OpenAlex first. Known primary sources were verified directly; supplementary web searches began after parent confirmed OpenAlex discovery was running.
review_metadata.scope: Sixteen core records include positive unpaired identification results and explicit causal biomedical challengers. This is not an exhaustive systematic review or a proof that all integration methods fail.
review_metadata.evidence_policy: Theorem statements and relevant methods were inspected in primary full texts. Formal proof correctness and implementations were not independently re-established for every publication. No new data, simulations, or fits were used.
review_metadata.funding_and_conflicts: Not extracted; theoretical applicability was assessed from observation contracts, target definitions, and assumptions.

records.title: Old and new approaches in statistical matching when samples are drawn with complex survey designs
records.publication_status: Istat-hosted author manuscript; publication year and venue not established from inspected copy
records.observation_contract: Distinct independent samples observe (X,Y) and (X,Z) from a common population.
records.target: Joint relationships among never-coobserved variables; identified sets rather than only sampling uncertainty.
records.assumptions: General block marginals do not determine the joint. Conditional independence or auxiliary restrictions can select a completion; complex survey designs require separate sampling treatment.
records.theorem_applicability: Direct context for the missing residual-coupling problem. Supports model-class-qualified nonidentification, not universal failure of restricted models.
records.evidence_locator: Author manuscript pp.1–2; §3 equations (5)–(6) define compatible joint distributions.
records.discovery_origin: prior focused review; direct primary retrieval

records.title: Unlinked Monotone Regression
records.observation_contract: Separate predictor and response samples; unlike shuffled regression they need not contain the same individuals or sample sizes.
records.target: A scalar monotone regression function, not an unrestricted multivariate causal DAG.
records.assumptions: Independent additive structural noise with known distribution; monotonicity; stated design/deconvolution regularity. Unknown-noise extensions use additional information.
records.theorem_applicability: Genuine recovery from unpaired marginals within a restricted model class. Known count-measurement noise does not automatically supply the required biological structural-noise law.
records.evidence_locator: Introduction pp.3–4; Assumption A0 §2.2; Theorems 1–5; §7 unknown-noise extensions.
records.discovery_origin: prior focused review; direct primary retrieval

records.title: Challenging Common Assumptions in the Unsupervised Learning of Disentangled Representations
records.observation_contract: Unsupervised observations from an unrestricted latent generative model; no informative auxiliary supervision.
records.assumptions: Dimension greater than one and a factorized latent density; the model class admits entangling bijections with identical observable distributions.
records.theorem_applicability: Related information argument, but not a theorem about original measured-variable DAGs or every structured multimodal model. Correct inductive restrictions can exclude alternatives.
records.evidence_locator: §3, Theorem 1 and following construction; Appendix A.

records.title: Nonlinear ICA Using Auxiliary Variables and Generalized Contrastive Learning
records.observation_contract: Each observed mixture accompanies an auxiliary variable such as time, history, or treatment label.
records.target: Latent components up to componentwise transformations; some exponential-family cases retain linear ambiguity.
records.assumptions: Conditional source independence, invertible smooth mixing/demixing, sufficiently diverse auxiliary modulation, and specified contrastive regression class.
records.theorem_applicability: Auxiliary information can identify sources under restrictions. An arbitrary integrated state or label does not automatically satisfy variability or independence, and sources are not a causal DAG.
records.evidence_locator: §4 Theorems 1–3; §5 warns against arbitrary auxiliary-variable construction.

records.title: Variational Autoencoders and Nonlinear ICA: A Unifying Framework
records.observation_contract: An observed mixture and auxiliary covariate are jointly available per sample.
records.target: Latent generative model/posterior equivalence class, not arbitrary original cross-assay causal edges.
records.assumptions: Injective mixing; conditionally factorized exponential-family latents; fixed observation-noise model with the characteristic-function condition; full-rank auxiliary modulation. Stronger equivalence needs further conditions.
records.theorem_applicability: A positive restricted identification result. Basic Theorem 1 permits linear sufficient-statistic ambiguity; ordinary multimodal VAEs do not inherit it merely by using a shared latent space.
records.evidence_locator: §4 Theorems 1–4; Proposition 1 covers unresolved Gaussian location-modulation ambiguity.

records.title: The Incomplete Rosetta Stone problem: Identifiability results for Multi-view Nonlinear ICA
records.publication_status: UAI 2019 proceedings published as PMLR 115:217–227 in 2020
records.observation_contract: Simultaneous views of the same source realization; contrastive learning distinguishes genuine joint tuples from shuffled tuples.
records.target: Shared independent sources or their corrupted versions, up to stated transformations.
records.assumptions: Invertible view mixing, componentwise independent corruption and sufficiently distinct views; noiseless/noisy/many-view results differ.
records.theorem_applicability: The true joint-view information differs from disjoint assay marginals. It cannot justify treating integration-generated pairs as observed positive pairs.
records.evidence_locator: §3 model equations (5)–(7), Theorems 1, 4, 5 and 8; §2 contrastive sampling.
records.discovery_origin: known primary source and central OpenAlex query06

records.title: Causal Discovery with Continuous Additive Noise Models
records.observation_contract: The joint distribution of all modeled observed variables is available.
records.target: The causal DAG, beyond its usual Markov equivalence class.
records.assumptions: Restricted additive-noise SEM, independent exogenous errors, causal minimality and the stated non-reversibility/regularity conditions.
records.theorem_applicability: Supports orientation after justified joint recovery. Additive neural equations alone are insufficient; the theorem does not recover missing cross-assay couplings.
records.evidence_locator: Definition 27 and Theorem 28; Condition 19; Examples 24 and 26.
records.discovery_origin: prior focused review; direct primary retrieval

records.title: Statistical Matching via Schrödinger Bridge beyond Conditional Independence
records.observation_contract: Partially overlapping (X,Y) and (X,Z) samples; reported tuning can additionally use complete auxiliary triplets.
records.target: Joint-distribution recovery and predictive completion, not causal orientation.
records.assumptions: Gaussian recovery theorem requires an oracle cost or residual-sign-compatible alignment cost and a suitable regularization parameter.
records.theorem_applicability: Existence of a recovering parameter is not identification of it from marginals. The oracle/sign restriction and parameter selection depend on missing joint information or extra assumptions.
records.evidence_locator: Theorem 3.2; §3.2 tuning discussion; Appendix A parameter formula and B.4 auxiliary-triplet validation.
records.discovery_origin: prior focused review and central OpenAlex query04

records.title: Statistical matching using fractional imputation
records.observation_contract: Independent samples measure common covariates with different outcomes.
records.target: Joint-model parameters and imputed joint analyses.
records.assumptions: A correctly specified identified parametric model. One sufficient construction uses instrumental-variable relevance and exclusion with a linear outcome equation.
records.theorem_applicability: Recovery can use restrictions rather than new measurements. IV validity is not guaranteed by a shared state. Numerical EM convergence alone should not be treated as a general identification proof.
records.evidence_locator: §2 Remark 2.1 and Example 2.1; §3 identified-model premise; §7 limitations. Final version differs from 2015 preprint wording.
records.discovery_origin: Koo reference snowball; central OpenAlex query04 preprint; supplementary publisher verification

openalex_related_records.relation: related preprint or earlier version; canonical metadata verified separately

records.title: Unpaired Multi-Domain Causal Representation Learning
records.observation_contract: Only separate domain marginals; no paired measurements or interventions required by the theorem.
records.target: The observed joint law is identified exactly; signed-block representation ambiguities leave that law invariant. The shared latent DAG is identified up to relabeling; its coefficients can retain sign ambiguities.
records.assumptions: Linear latent SEM and full-column-rank linear views, with no unspecified extra count kernel; independent distinct nonsymmetric standardized errors. Graph recovery needs separated shared/private blocks, two partial pure children per shared latent and rank faithfulness.
records.theorem_applicability: A genuine counterexample to blanket impossibility from unpaired data. Its restricted model excludes the Gaussian counterfamily; it does not establish arbitrary feature-level regulation from raw counts.
records.evidence_locator: Official PDF: Eq. (1)–(2) and Definition 2.1, pp4–5; C1–C2 and Theorem 3.1, p6; Definition 4.2 and C3–C4, pp7–8; Theorem 4.4, p8; Remark 3.3 and Appendix C.
records.discovery_origin: central OpenAlex query05 and supplementary primary search
records.measurement_scope: Domain-private latent factors can represent noise within this model; appending Poisson/negative-binomial observations is not licensed by the theorem without another identification argument.
records.joint_graph_scope_distinction: Remark 3.3 permits shared-to-private directed paths for joint-law identification, but no private-to-shared paths. Section 4 uses separated shared/private blocks for its shared-graph identification theorem.

records.title: Identifiable Shared Component Analysis of Unpaired Multimodal Mixtures
records.observation_contract: Unpaired linear mixtures of common and private components; separate variants add identical mixing structure or a few paired anchors.
records.target: Aligned shared components up to a common invertible linear transform; stronger ICA variants recover individual components.
records.assumptions: Full-column-rank mixing, full-rank shared covariance, modality variability and restrictions removing distribution-preserving ambiguities; anchor variants have different assumptions.
records.theorem_applicability: Unpaired distribution matching can be identifiable within restricted models. The shared-subspace result is not a theorem identifying arbitrary residual couplings or a causal DAG.
records.evidence_locator: Official PDF: Eq. (1), §2; Assumption 1 and Theorem 1, pp4–5; Corollary 1, p5; additional same-mixing and paired-anchor variants in §4, pp6–7; Appendix H private components.
records.discovery_origin: central OpenAlex query06 and supplementary primary search

records.title: Causal Representation Learning from Multimodal Biomedical Observations
records.publication_status: ICLR 2025; proceedings verified despite PMC copy being labeled preprint
records.observation_contract: Theorems compare complete multimodal joint laws p(x), and the estimator uses jointly observed modality tuples.
records.target: Latent subspaces/components connected across modalities; graph estimates evaluated empirically.
records.assumptions: Smooth invertible generating maps, sufficient cross-modality influence/Jacobian rank and a structural sparsity condition excluding denser mixed representations.
records.theorem_applicability: A relevant nonlinear biomedical positive result with a different observation contract. Replacing joint tuples by integration-generated pairs is not covered by its theorem.
records.evidence_locator: Official PDF: Conditions 4.1/4.3 and Theorems 4.2/4.4, pp4–7; §5 joint estimation, pp8–9; proofs Appendix C. Theorem 4.4 explicitly assumes equality of full p(x).
records.discovery_origin: central OpenAlex query05; supplementary PMC and ICLR verification

records.title: Causal integration of multi-omics data with prior knowledge to generate mechanistic hypotheses
records.observation_contract: Bulk multi-omics tumor/normal contrasts with biological sample correspondence and a signed directed prior network.
records.target: Coherent mechanistic hypotheses selected from prior pathways.
records.assumptions: Curated regulatory signs/directions and activity footprints; optimization favors compact networks explaining measured changes.
records.theorem_applicability: Additional directed biological knowledge changes the information contract. Authors frame outputs as hypotheses, not complete de novo causal identification.
records.evidence_locator: Introduction; Fig.1; Discussion limitations; Methods prior-network construction and CARNIVAL optimization.

records.title: Propensity Score Alignment of Unpaired Multimodal Data
records.publication_status: NeurIPS 37 (2024), main conference; official proceedings verified
records.observation_contract: Separate modalities with observed experimental labels perturbing a shared latent state.
records.target: A common identifiable propensity representation and matching/prediction, not a causal DAG.
records.assumptions: Injective modality measurement maps and treatment-independent private variation conditional on state; sufficiently informative perturbations for full state discrimination.
records.theorem_applicability: A relevant biological alignment result using permitted information only if such labels and assumptions exist. Equal propensity scores need not imply equal states; residual causality is not identified by alignment alone.
records.evidence_locator: §2; Propositions 3.1–3.2; Appendix A explicitly separates shuffled same-source data.

records.title: Integrating Optimal Transport and Structural Inference Models for GRN Inference from Single-cell Data
records.publication_status: ECML PKDD 2024 proceedings, CCIS2560, pp257–271; first online 7 May 2026
records.observation_contract: Known temporal snapshots of the same jointly measured gene panel; reported simulations shuffle existing trajectories at sampled times.
records.target: A gene regulatory graph inferred from transport-reconstructed trajectories.
records.assumptions: Temporal ordering, chosen transport geometry and a dynamical structural-inference model.
records.theorem_applicability: A meaningful empirical challenger in a different design, not an identification theorem for disjoint modalities at one population snapshot. No general identifiability theorem was found in the inspected text.
records.evidence_locator: Publisher 2026 metadata/abstract verified; full methods inspected in 2024 preprint: §3 OT trajectory construction; §4 structural inference; §5.1 shuffled temporal benchmark design. Final publisher full text is subscription gated.
records.discovery_origin: parent referral from independent integration-method reviewer

records.title: Causal Discovery from Heterogeneous/Nonstationary Data
records.observation_contract: Jointly measured variables with a domain or time index across changing distributions.
records.target: Causal skeleton and directions supported by changes; otherwise an equivalence class.
records.assumptions: Pseudo causal sufficiency, augmented faithfulness and independent mechanism changes/edge-specific conditions for orientation.
records.theorem_applicability: Heterogeneity can add identifying information under explicit restrictions. Batch labels or independently missing cross-assay variables do not automatically supply the required joint conditional tests.
